title: California 1939 and the burning of the Pid-mor Ballroom
summary: Jones describes the 1939 California trip and says a ballroom was burned down rather than let a black band play, then the Paramount and Treasure Island fair.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What was the beginning of the 40's like with you, Jo? Do you remember?
Oh, sure...J: In 1939 we went to California. We were supposed to open up at the Ball Room where Mr. Benny Goodman had played. Charlie Barnet was playing in the Ball Room in 1939.
Do you remember the name of the Ball-Room? Was it the Million Dollar Ball-Room?...

They burned the Pid-mor Ball-Room down. They burned it down including Mr. Charlie Barnet's instruments and all of his music because they did not want a black band to play out there where Benny Goodman had got his big smash out there. When we were playing in the Oakland Ball-Room, we came into Los Angeles, we did 18 days down in the theatre and they took us and we played the World's Fair up in San Francisco on Treasure Island. They had the Peters Sisters and Bonnie Baker was with Tommy Tucker... They burned the place down rather than have a black musician come to play.
That's the Pid-mor and now we're in 'Frisco, at The World's Fair. That wasn't where they burned it down.
We left from doing 18 days in the theatre, the Paramount Theatre - we left and then we went up there and we played at the Fair.
